newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Placer says Porgera back to capacity.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Placer says Porgera back to capacity.

text.p: The joint venture partners at the Porgera gold mine in the highlands of Papua New Guinea said on Friday that the mine had returned to full milling capacity following lengthy dry weather.
They said May gold production was little affected by the water shortage but production in June was about 30 percent of forecast.
The mine produces about onE million ounces of gold each year.
"Stockpiled high grade ore is being preferentially fed to the mill to offset as much of the lost production as possible," the partners said.
Placer Dome Inc, which is the operator of the mine, has a 50 percent stake. The other equal stakes are held by Goldfields Ltd and Orogen Minerals Ltd which is majority-owned by the PNG government.
Milling operations were suspended on June 1 due to lengthy dry weather which sharply lowered water reserves at they Waile Creek Dam which supplies the mine.
Recent rain had replenished water reserves at the dam which was now close to full. Additional water would continue to be drawn from smaller nearby sources.
"Water reserve levels will continue to be monitored closely as the Porgera area has entered what is traditionally its drier period of the year," the partners said.
